intro: を marks the noun that an action passes over: the thing the action works on (本を読む), the ground a movement covers (道を歩く), or the place it leaves behind (家を出る). It always belongs to a verb, never to an adjective or a noun. It is written with the old kana を, which today is used only for this particle, and is pronounced "o".

skills.rule: The thing a transitive verb does something to takes を.
skills.explain:
If the verb is done to something (eat it, read it, open it, make it, study it), that something takes を: パンを食べる, 窓を開ける, 宿題をする. Ask "what?" of the verb; the answer is the を noun.

Many ideas that are transitive in English are not verbs of doing in Japanese and take が: 好き, 嫌い, 上手, ほしい, 分かる, できる, 要る, 見える, 聞こえる. Others take に for the person or thing you go towards: 友達に会う, バスに乗る, 母に電話する. Learn these as fixed frames.

Japanese has many verb pairs: 開ける (open something) takes を, 開く (come open) takes が. ドアを開ける, ドアが開く. The same goes for 閉める / 閉まる, 始める / 始まる, つける / つく.

A noun + する verb takes one を only: 日本語を勉強する or 日本語の勉強をする, never 日本語を勉強をする. When the object becomes the topic or gets も, を disappears: 肉は食べません, 肉も食べます (not をは, をも). In casual speech を is often simply dropped.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]本[ほん]{を}読[よ]みました。
窓[まど]{を}開[あ]けてください。
母[はは]は毎朝[まいあさ]お弁当[べんとう]{を}作[つく]ります。
examples.en: My mother makes a packed lunch every morning.

examples.jp: 毎晩[まいばん]日本語[にほんご]{を}勉強[べんきょう]しています。
誰[だれ]がこの絵[え]{を}描[か]きましたか。

contrast.note: が marks the object of states and feelings (好き, ほしい, 分かる, できる) and the subject of intransitive verbs: ドアが開く "the door opens" against ドアを開ける "I open the door".
Some verbs aim at a person or thing rather than act on it and take に: 先生に会う, 電車に乗る, 友達に電話する. With を these are wrong.
で marks the tool or place of the action, not what it acts on: 箸でご飯を食べる "eat rice with chopsticks". The thing eaten is を; the means is で.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]{を}会[あ]いました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]{に}会[あ]いました。
mistakes.note: 会う takes に for the person you meet, even though English "meet" is transitive.

mistakes.bad: 少[すこ]し日本語[にほんご]{を}分[わ]かります。
mistakes.good: 少[すこ]し日本語[にほんご]{が}分[わ]かります。
mistakes.note: 分かる is a state verb ("be understandable"); what is understood takes が, as with できる and 好き.
開く is intransitive ("came open") and takes が; to open something yourself, use the transitive 開ける with を.

skills.tip: Can you say "I did it to the noun"? Then を. If the word is a feeling, an ability or something that just happens, reach for が.

skills.rule: The space a movement goes through, along or across takes を with verbs of motion.
skills.explain:
With motion verbs such as 歩く, 走る, 通る, 渡る, 飛ぶ, 散歩する and 曲がる, を marks the route: the road you walk along, the bridge you cross, the sky a bird flies through, the corner you turn. These verbs are intransitive, but を is still correct, because the noun is the ground the movement covers.

を tells you nothing about where the movement ends. A goal takes に or へ: 道を渡る "cross the road", 向こう側に渡る "cross over to the other side". Both can appear together: 次の角を右に曲がる "turn right at the next corner" (the corner is the route, 右 is the direction).

The edge with で: で marks a venue where an activity happens as a whole, with no sense of covering ground. 公園で遊ぶ "play in the park", but 公園を散歩する "take a walk around the park". プールで泳ぐ is swimming at the pool; 川を泳いで渡る is swimming across the river.
patterns: [road / bridge / park] を [歩く / 渡る / 散歩する]

examples.jp: この橋[はし]{を}渡[わた]ってください。
毎朝[まいあさ]この道[みち]{を}歩[ある]きます。
examples.en: I walk along this road every morning.

examples.jp: 犬[いぬ]と公園[こうえん]{を}散歩[さんぽ]しました。
examples.en: I took a walk around the park with my dog.

examples.jp: 鳥[とり]が空[そら]{を}飛[と]んでいます。
examples.en: Birds are flying across the sky.

examples.jp: 次[つぎ]の角[かど]{を}右[みぎ]に曲[ま]がってください。
examples.en: Please turn right at the next corner.

examples.jp: このバスは駅前[えきまえ]{を}通[とお]りますか。
examples.en: Does this bus go past the station?

contrast.note: で is the venue of an activity, not ground covered: 公園で遊ぶ "play in the park" against 公園を走る "run through the park".
に and へ mark where the movement ends up: 道を渡る "cross the road" against 向こう側に渡る "go over to the other side".

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]の橋[はし]{に}渡[わた]りました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]の橋[はし]{を}渡[わた]りました。
mistakes.note: The bridge is what you cross, not where you arrive; に would need a destination such as 向こう側に.

mistakes.bad: 日曜日[にちようび]に公園[こうえん]{に}散歩[さんぽ]しました。
mistakes.good: 日曜日[にちようび]に公園[こうえん]{を}散歩[さんぽ]しました。
mistakes.note: The park is the area you walk around, so を; に is only right with a verb of going: 公園に散歩に行く.

skills.tip: Picture the movement as a line drawn over the noun. If the line runs along or across it, を; if the noun is just a box where something happens, で.

skills.rule: The place or vehicle you leave, step out of or get off takes を with verbs of leaving.
skills.explain:
Verbs of leaving, 出る, 降りる, 出発する, 離れる and 卒業する, mark the place left behind with を: 家を出る "leave home", 電車を降りる "get off the train", 国を離れる "leave one's country". It is the mirror image of に with verbs of entering: 部屋に入る / 部屋を出る, バスに乗る / バスを降りる.

から is also possible for physical leaving (部屋から出る, 電車から降りる) and puts more weight on the starting point of the motion, especially with a destination or てくる: 猫が箱から出てきた. For abstract leaving only を works: 大学を卒業する, 大学を出る "graduate", 会社を辞める. を also needs a mover that leaves; for something that merely comes out, only から works: 煙が窓から出る, not 窓を出る.

Do not use に for the place you leave. に with 降りる marks where you land: ホームに降りる "step down onto the platform". The station where you get off takes で: 次の駅で電車を降りる.
patterns: [place] を 出る / 出発する

examples.jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]八時[はちじ]に家[いえ]{を}出[で]ます。
examples.en: I leave home at eight every morning.

examples.jp: 次[つぎ]の駅[えき]で電車[でんしゃ]{を}降[お]ります。
examples.en: I get off the train at the next station.

examples.jp: 部屋[へや]{を}出[で]るときは電気[でんき]を消[け]してください。
examples.en: Please turn off the light when you leave the room.

examples.jp: 姉[あね]は去年[きょねん]大学[だいがく]{を}卒業[そつぎょう]しました。
examples.en: My older sister graduated from university last year.

examples.jp: 飛行機[ひこうき]は十時[じゅうじ]に空港[くうこう]{を}出発[しゅっぱつ]しました。
examples.en: The plane left the airport at ten.

examples.jp: 十八歳[じゅうはっさい]のときに国[くに]{を}離[はな]れました。
examples.en: I left my country when I was eighteen.

contrast.note: から stresses the starting point and is common for physical exits (部屋から出てくる), but abstract leaving such as 卒業する takes only を.
に points the other way: 電車に乗る "get on", 電車を降りる "get off". With 降りる, に is the surface you land on, never the vehicle you leave.
で marks where the leaving happens, not what is left: 駅で電車を降りる "get off the train at the station".

mistakes.bad: 次[つぎ]の駅[えき]で電車[でんしゃ]{に}降[お]ります。
mistakes.good: 次[つぎ]の駅[えき]で電車[でんしゃ]{を}降[お]ります。
mistakes.note: You get on a train with に but get off it with を (or から); に is for the vehicle you board.

mistakes.bad: 去年[きょねん]大学[だいがく]{から}卒業[そつぎょう]しました。
mistakes.good: 去年[きょねん]大学[だいがく]{を}卒業[そつぎょう]しました。
mistakes.note: English says "graduate from", but 卒業する takes を for the school; から does not fit abstract leaving.

mistakes.bad: 七時[しちじ]に家[いえ]{で}出[で]ました。
mistakes.good: 七時[しちじ]に家[いえ]{を}出[で]ました。
mistakes.note: The house is the place left, not the place where an action is carried out, so を, not で.

skills.tip: Leaving is the reverse of entering: where entering takes に (入る, 乗る), leaving takes を (出る, 降りる).
